About audiation

Audiation is hearing music in your head, with understanding, even when the sound is gone or was never there.

What the word means

Edwin E. Gordon used audiation for the musical equivalent of thinking in language. When someone speaks, you hold sounds until they become words. In music you organise what you just heard, and predict what may come, from key and metre.

Hearing with the ears (aural perception) happens while the sound arrives. Audiation is the cognitive follow-up: giving meaning. Without that, music stays a chain of stimuli, or copying fingers.

What this app is and is not

The Audiation app leans on that idea — inner hearing — in its own simple path of twelve steps, from about age 7. It is not a Music Learning Theory course, not GIML certification, and not a substitute for a teacher. Names (Do or 1) come after hearing, except when finding a note. Singing or an instrument is a check, not the goal.

If you want to go further, toward Gordon and Music Learning Theory, a short list is below. Those sites belong to others; I do not run them.
